producer_report.summary: Athena now runs the error review backfill and the evidence-label derivation by itself at the start of every drain (before the queue is read) and in every hestia sweep, and prints one summary line for each. A failing pass is reported in its line and stops nothing. Root cause of the label churn: the recurrence-after-prevention basis detail held the live count of closed jobs, so each newly closed job made a different basis and derive() wrote a fresh label. The detail now states the threshold (at least STOPPED_MIN_JOBS closed jobs), so it is the same text whenever the evidence is the same. Added Athena::review_passes and hestia_sweep_with in hestia.rs, and a Steps::review_passes hook with a no-op default that RealSteps implements. The hestia sweep command calls hestia_sweep_with with the terminal UI. Doc comments and the status hint were reworded to say Athena runs these passes. A CHANGELOG entry notes it supersedes request 20261026-224929-6erm. Closing that request is left to the landing process.

learnings: derive() skips a rewrite only when the class and the full LabelBasis (including the detail text) are equal, so any live number in the basis detail makes labels unstable.
Terminal UI lines go to stderr, so adding summary lines to the hestia sweep command does not disturb its --json output on stdout.
The ClassLabel basis detail for the 'recurred' variant still contains the number of later recurrences. That is a change in the evidence, so it is correct for it to change.
desires: A way to read a persisted large tool output inside the working directory, so a long test run can be checked for failures.
